key_insight: NeuMesh++ introduces a mesh-based neural representation that disentangles geometry, texture, and semantic information, making volumetric scene editing more flexible and efficient. This enables richer edits than prior methods that were limited to rigid transforms or narrow, category-specific operations.
problem_solved: Existing neural rendering/editing methods are often too restrictive for practical scene manipulation, supporting only limited edits such as rigid movement or object-category-specific changes. NeuMesh++ addresses the need for a general-purpose, editable 3D representation that can support versatile volumetric editing.
method: Encodes a neural radiance field on mesh vertices instead of relying solely on dense volumetric representations.
Separates the representation into disentangled geometry, texture, and semantic codes to support targeted edits.
Uses the mesh structure to improve efficiency while preserving implicit-field expressiveness for reconstruction and editing.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more practical path to editable 3D content creation, simulation, and scene reconstruction. It can reduce edit complexity while enabling more controllable and scalable volumetric manipulation.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing input 3D scene → mesh-based encoding → editable outputs.

paper_title: NeuMesh++: Towards Versatile and Efficient Volumetric Editing with Disentangled Neural Mesh-based Implicit Field
paper_authors: Chong Bao, Yuan Li, Bangbang Yang, Yujun Shen, Hujun Bao
